The proposed answer is wrong. My derivation gives $(2/d)^{d/(d-2)}$, which is not $1/d$ (for $d=3$ it gives $8/27 \approx 0.296$, not $1/3$).

**Derivation sketch.** Root the tree at $v$. Each neighbor $u$ has $k=d-1$ children in its branch. Let $T_u$ be the time $u$ is eliminated by its own branch, and let $\tau_w \sim \mathrm{Exp}(1)$ be the clock of edge $(u,w)$. The edge game between $u$ and child $w$ matters only if $w$ is still alive at $\tau_w$, which happens when $T_w > \tau_w$. Then $u$ is eliminated with probability $1/2$. So define
$$X_w = \tau_w \cdot \mathbf{1}\{\text{coin favors } w,\ T_w>\tau_w\}\quad(\text{with } X_w=\infty \text{ otherwise}),$$
and $T_u = \min_{w} X_w$ over the $k$ children. The root survives iff all $d$ of its neighbors' $X$-values are infinite, and these are independent.

Let $S(t)=P(T>t)$ and $H(t)=P(X\le t)$. Then
$$H(t)=\tfrac12\int_0^t e^{-s}S(s)\,ds,\qquad S=(1-H)^k.$$
Writing $s=1-H$ gives $s^{1-k}=1+\tfrac{k-1}{2}(1-e^{-t})$. Hence
$$P(X=\infty)=s(\infty)=\left(\tfrac{k+1}{2}\right)^{-1/(k-1)}=\left(\tfrac d2\right)^{-1/(d-2)}.$$
Therefore
$$P(v\text{ active})=P(X=\infty)^d=\left(\tfrac{2}{d}\right)^{d/(d-2)}.$$

**Checks.** As $d\to 2^+$ this tends to $e^{-1}$, which matches the direct path computation $s(\infty)=e^{-1/2}$ per neighbor. The formula is also undefined at $d=2$ as a closed form, consistent with the problem's restriction to $d>2$. The proposed argument is heuristic and never actually computes the probability.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
